issues.summary: services/ is a flat 29k-LOC package with no capability boundaries
issues.suggestion: Split services/ into purpose-named subpackages (orchestration, benchmarking, persistence, reporting, host_lifecycle) and move modules; preserve public import paths with a temporary facade.
evidence: 251 structural issues are attributed to lm_optimizer/services.
The directory mixes phase orchestration, benchmarking, reporting, host lifecycle and UI support.

issues.summary: domain/models.py is a 112-importer hub that combines every aggregate
issues.suggestion: Split domain/models.py by aggregate (hardware.py, configuration.py, benchmark.py, run.py) and re-export from domain/__init__.py during migration.
evidence: The file defines hardware, model identity, benchmark cases, load configuration, quality scores, runs and profile weights in 683 LOC.
Any change to one model forces a rebuild of the import graph for 112 modules.

issues.summary: discovery/ still crosses into the legacy api/client module
issues.suggestion: Port inspector.py to the service client; then retire api/client.py or clearly mark it as a test-only compatibility module.
evidence: inspector.py imports LMStudioClient, LoadConfig and ModelInfo from api.client.
The current host client lives in services/lm_studio.py.

issues.summary: cli/main.py mixes command parsing with application orchestration and rendering
issues.suggestion: Extract preflight/host lifecycle into services and move command bodies into cli/commands/* modules; keep main.py to Typer registration and output composition.
evidence: The file is 5,718 LOC and contains the 603-line optimize and auto command bodies, 244-line preflight, and 362-line result renderer.
Preflight, host lifecycle and report generation are reusable operations but live inside the CLI module.

issues.suggestion: Group services by capability and make each subpackage expose a small __init__ API.
evidence: A single flat directory contains orchestration, benchmark execution, report rendering, host defaults and recommendation logic.
Structural debt by area reports 251 items in lm_optimizer/services.

issues.summary: API handlers translate the same underlying failures into ad-hoc HTTP responses
issues.suggestion: Add a single exception-to-HTTP mapping layer or middleware and use typed domain exceptions; keep detail strings out of 500 responses.
evidence: Handlers catch Exception and raise HTTPException with status 500 and truncated str(e) in several places.
Other handlers let exceptions propagate to FastAPI defaults, producing a different response shape.

issues.summary: API conversion helpers only forward fields into schemas
issues.suggestion: Use Pydantic model_validate with from_attributes=True or schema constructors at the boundary, and keep only conversions that add policy (masking secrets, deriving metrics).
evidence: _convert_model, _convert_hardware, _convert_config and _convert_preset are thin field-by-field mappers.
They add a second place to update whenever a domain field changes.

issues.summary: Config/defaults modules rely on dict[str, Any] instead of typed structures
issues.suggestion: Introduce TypedDicts or dataclasses for the LM Studio defaults document and duel payloads; keep raw dicts only at the JSON edge.
evidence: lmstudio_defaults.py has 23 dict[str, Any] annotations; duel.py 11; hostguard.py 8.
Key names are string literals repeated across read/merge/apply/restore functions.

issues.summary: CLI command bodies mix parsing, preflight, orchestration and rendering
issues.suggestion: Extract one function per phase (prepare, execute, persist, render) and keep the command body as a short composition; pass a small prepared-context object instead of a dozen locals.
evidence: optimize and auto are each 603 lines; _auto is 402 and _display_optimization_result is 362.
Each body performs several side-effecting phases sequentially with shared local state.

issues.summary: Report generation is one 531-line function with many inline formatting branches
issues.suggestion: Split into section builders that each return lines, then compose them in save_best_report; this keeps formatting testable without changing output.
evidence: save_best_report builds every section (header, config table, quality, ladder, presets, diagnostics) in one body.
Section formatting is interleaved with data lookup and fallback handling.

issues.summary: Async functions perform blocking work without awaits
issues.suggestion: Move blocking repository/file work to asyncio.to_thread or a background task where it can delay the event loop; keep pure in-memory work inline.
evidence: Several async handlers call synchronous repository/file helpers directly.
Long CPU-bound preparation runs on the event loop instead of a thread.

issues.summary: API response mapping is split between converters and dict enrichment
issues.suggestion: Move enrichment into the schema/converter or a single presenter function, and return one response shape per resource.
evidence: _convert_config_result builds a schema, then _enrich_config_detail mutates its dict form with extra keys.
Different endpoints apply different subsets of enrichment.

issues.summary: Docstrings on long functions describe only one responsibility
issues.suggestion: Either split the function so the docstring is accurate, or expand it to list all side effects and outputs.
evidence: save_best_report is documented as saving a report but also builds diagnostics, presets and ladder sections.
_test_config documents loading but also benchmarks, scores and cleans up.

issues.summary: Command functions own several distinct responsibilities
issues.suggestion: Extract a shared optimization workflow service and keep CLI commands as thin adapters that parse input and render results.
evidence: optimize/auto combine argument validation, preflight, host lifecycle, run execution and report rendering.
The same responsibilities are also implemented in the API path.

issues.summary: _test_config combines load, benchmark, quality and persistence
issues.suggestion: Split into load_candidate, measure_candidate, evaluate_candidate and record_candidate steps composed by _test_config.
evidence: The 244-line function loads a model, runs cases, evaluates quality, records results and cleans up in one body.
Failure handling for each stage is interleaved.

issues.summary: Public helpers annotated -> dict return different key sets by branch
issues.suggestion: Return Pydantic models or TypedDicts with required/optional fields, and keep raw dicts only at serialization boundaries.
evidence: Several handlers and default helpers return dict with optional keys added conditionally.
Callers use .get(...) because the annotation does not promise a shape.

issues.summary: Docstrings describe the happy path but omit raised errors
issues.suggestion: Add Raises/Returns sections for public functions and align annotations with every return path.
evidence: Client methods raise on transport errors without a documented Raises section.
Some service helpers return None/False for invalid input instead of raising.

issues.summary: Most service parameters and returns lack annotations
issues.suggestion: Annotate public entrypoints first (prepare_run, execute, run_cases, auto_run) with concrete types and enable mypy/pyright on those modules.
evidence: The AST census finds 693 unannotated parameters and 264 unannotated returns.
Public service methods accept advanced settings and config fragments as bare dicts.

add.description: backends/base.py defines BackendClient and assert_conforms, and OllamaClient implements the seam; backend-specific code is not spread through the domain.
web_main.py launches api.main:app, and ui/web.py is explicitly marked as deprecated reference code, so the current entrypoint is unambiguous.
The deprecated ui/web.py docstring names api.main:app as authoritative, which prevents a new engineer from wiring the wrong app.
OptimizationPhase/OptimizationStage enumerate the pipeline stages instead of relying on implicit string flow, which gives the orchestration a readable spine.
BenchmarkService records success=False and an error per case instead of aborting the whole sweep, which keeps one bad prompt from losing a run.
Cancellation paths explicitly checkpoint state before unwinding, preserving recoverability across failures.
The BackendClient protocol is implemented by OllamaClient and exercised by conformance checks, so the abstraction has more than one consumer.
Functions such as parse_phase_skips and compose_granular_skips encode real skip semantics rather than forwarding arguments.
Helpers such as _looks_incomplete, _sample_mem and _extract_mtp_metrics are short, side-effect-light and easy to test.
The optimizer exposes ordered phases and skip names, so the CLI/API handoff for phase control is at least named and testable.
The 2.5% comment ratio and short docstrings avoid restating code; comments generally explain constraints or intent.
AdaptiveOptimizer runs named phases (speed, context speed, quality, recovery, validation) with explicit skip handling, which is a coherent orchestration spine.
Core domain dataclasses expose to_dict/from_dict pairs and are exercised by round-trip tests, giving persistence a reliable contract.
Domain dataclasses and Pydantic schemas type the main entities (runs, configs, metrics, requests), giving the persistence and HTTP layers a reliable core.
